understand.concept: Regex flags change how a pattern is interpreted. IGNORECASE removes case distinctions, MULTILINE changes line-anchor behaviour, DOTALL lets dot match newline characters, and VERBOSE allows readable whitespace and comments. For validating a complete input, fullmatch is clearer than a loose substring search. Pattern design should avoid excessive backtracking on untrusted input.
understand.whyItMatters: Flags make patterns adaptable, while full-input validation and bounded patterns reduce accidental acceptance and performance risks.
understand.analogy: Flags are operating settings for a search tool; they change how the same pattern reads the text.
understand.analogyLimit: Regex validation cannot replace semantic checks, and a pattern that is safe on short sample text may behave poorly on very long or adversarial input.
understand.summary: Regex Flags, Full-Input Validation and Safe Pattern Design teaches readable and predictable pattern matching with Python's re module.

explain.narrative:
## Flags and safer validation
Pass flags such as `re.IGNORECASE`, `re.MULTILINE`, `re.DOTALL` or `re.VERBOSE` to a regex operation or compile call. Combine flags with bitwise OR when needed. VERBOSE patterns can include whitespace and comments to make complex expressions maintainable.

Use `fullmatch()` when the entire input must satisfy a format. Keep quantifiers bounded where possible, avoid ambiguous nested repetition, and limit input length before matching untrusted data. A regex is not a complete validator for domain rules such as whether a date actually exists.

examples.title: Ignore letter case
examples.explanation: IGNORECASE makes matching independent of letter case.

examples.title: Use multiline anchors
examples.code:
import re
text = 'alpha\nbeta'
print(re.findall(r'^\w+', text, flags=re.MULTILINE))
examples.explanation: MULTILINE makes ^ match the beginning of each line.

examples.title: Let dot include newlines
examples.code:
import re
text = 'start\nmiddle\nend'
print(bool(re.search(r'start.*end', text, flags=re.DOTALL)))
examples.explanation: DOTALL allows dot to match newline characters.

examples.title: Write a readable verbose pattern
examples.code:
import re
pattern = re.compile(r'''\d{4}  # year
    -\d{2} # month''', re.VERBOSE)
print(bool(pattern.fullmatch('2026-11')))
examples.explanation: VERBOSE ignores unescaped pattern whitespace and comments outside character classes.

examples.title: Validate a complete bounded code
examples.explanation: fullmatch rejects trailing text instead of accepting only a valid substring.
